correctness.notes: oracle passed on every measured cell | 78 cells dropped for lack of a control value (a cell-list batch run under the other requirement carries the same cells without the reference's path, their twins with a control are in the card), for example N32 k16 bf16 prefer_smaller_index latency | phase 3 final evaluation, harness 0.10, nodes umbriel-b200-047, umbriel-b200-068 | cells come from more than one node, see the node field of every cell: umbriel-b200-047, umbriel-b200-068

low_level: Registers 19 to 255 over the 476 distinct kernels behind the card's cells (34 with register spills, a kernel measured in more than one batch counts once), shared memory 48 to 65568 bytes, harness 0.10 on umbriel-b200-047, umbriel-b200-068.
Adapter statics: input arrangement blocked, output indices, temp storage 4 to 4 bytes.
Oracle battery (23 cases per cell plus the measurement seeds) passed on every cell that has a number, no cell unsupported, no cell failed the oracle.
algorithmic: Random input (the one-node matrix on umbriel-b200-047): latency not_guaranteed wins 42 of 89 cells (runner-up in 19), latency prefer_smaller_index wins 26 of 70 cells (runner-up in 18), throughput not_guaranteed wins 21 of 87 cells (runner-up in 30), throughput prefer_smaller_index wins 9 of 70 cells (runner-up in 26).

Where it wins on random input (bf16 N 32, bf16 N 128, bf16 N 160, bf16 N 256, bf16 N 384, bf16 N 512, bf16 N 768, bf16 N 896 and more), the median margin over the runner-up is +52 percent and over the scope's reference control +701 percent.

Largest random-input deficits (distinct cells, worst regime): fp32 N 2048 k 1024 +932 percent behind W3_d4c in latency prefer_smaller_index, bf16 N 2048 k 1024 +914 percent behind W3_d4c in latency not_guaranteed, bf16 N 4096 k 1024 +619 percent behind N5_rows_f in throughput not_guaranteed, fp32 N 4096 k 1024 +597 percent behind W3_d4c in throughput not_guaranteed.

Tie-heavy input (unshuffled, umbriel-b200-068): latency not_guaranteed wins 17 of 42 cells (runner-up in 9), latency prefer_smaller_index wins 15 of 39 cells (runner-up in 9), throughput not_guaranteed wins 11 of 42 cells (runner-up in 7), throughput prefer_smaller_index wins 11 of 39 cells (runner-up in 5).

Named workloads won on random input: deepseek_v3_final_top8, eagle2_children_top10, moba_1m_b4096_top12, moe_deepseek_v3_256, moe_ernie45, moe_glm45, moe_kimi_k2_384, moe_kimi_k3_896_top16, moe_longcat_768_top12, moe_nemotron3_ultra_512_top22, moe_qwen35_512_top10, moe_qwen3_128, moe_step3_padded, nsa_blocks_32k, peer_candidate_top16, peer_subkey_top16.

surprises: None beyond what the tables show.
open_questions: Whether the fp32 route can carry the full key for the last compare without losing the packed round.

GB200 pass on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99 (WINNERS_gb200.md): the warp and sub-warp winners agree on 359 of 376 common cells (365 of 376 when each cell is compared through the adapters both passes measured, as section 16 of the knowledge base does), the differences are named sub-warp lane-count cells, N 128 sub-warp throughput cells and warp ties within 5 percent, and in the block matrices the B1_idx against B1_det2 throughput ties fall either way.
